title: Keto Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Keto Calculator: Daily calories and keto macros — fat, protein and carbs in grams. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to…
content:
The [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Daily calories and keto macros — fat, protein and carbs in grams. Enter your sex, age, height, weight, activity level, goal and keto ratio (fat / protein / carbs) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Work out your daily calories and keto macros: how many grams of fat, protein and net carbs to eat on a ketogenic diet. The calculator finds your maintenance calories from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, adjusts for your goal, then splits the calories by your chosen ratio — usually 70% fat, 25% protein and 5% carbs. A keto diet keeps carbs low enough (usually under 50 g a day) that the body burns fat for fuel. This is an estimate for healthy adults, not medical advice. It does not suit children, pregnancy, eating disorders or anyone with a medical condition — talk to a doctor or registered dietitian before changing your diet or sleep habits.

## How to use the Keto Calculator

Start by choosing your sex from the list, then entering your age, entering your height (cm), entering your weight (kg), choosing your activity level from the list, choosing your goal from the list and finally choosing your keto ratio (fat / protein / carbs) from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your sex, age, height, weight and activity level.
2. Choose your goal and your keto ratio — 70/25/5 is the standard one.
3. Read your daily calories and the grams of fat, protein and net carbs.

## Formula

BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor): men 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5; women the same with −161. Maintenance = BMR × activity factor; lose weight × 0.8, gain weight × 1.1. Fat grams = calories × fat% ÷ 9; protein and carb grams = calories × % ÷ 4.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 30-year-old man, 175 cm, 80 kg, moderately active: maintenance is about 2,711 kcal a day. On the standard 70/25/5 ratio that is 211 g of fat, 169 g of protein and 34 g of net carbs a day. Try the same figures in the [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Sex: Male, Age: 30, Height: 175 cm, Weight: 80 kg, Activity level: Moderate (3–5 days/week), Goal: Maintain weight, Keto ratio (fat / protein / carbs): 70% fat / 25% protein / 5% carbs (standard)), the [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) returns Daily calories: 2,711 kcal, Fat: 211 g / day (70% of calories), Protein: 169 g / day (25% of calories), Net carbs: 34 g / day (5% of calories), Maintenance calories: 2,711 kcal / day. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## What keto actually is

A ketogenic diet is very low in carbohydrates (usually under 50 g of net carbs a day) and high in fat, with moderate protein. With almost no glucose coming in, the liver turns fat into ketones, which the brain and body burn instead. It takes a few days to adapt — the “keto flu” of tiredness and headaches is common in the first week — and the diet is a medical treatment for epilepsy, so anyone with a medical condition should talk to a doctor first.

## Protein matters more than the ratio

The fat/protein/carb ratio is a guide, not a law. The number that matters most is protein: too little and you lose muscle along with fat, too much and the extra can slow ketosis. A common target is 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kilogram of body weight a day. Fat is the flexible part — eat enough to feel full, and less of it if you want to lose weight faster, since body fat makes up the difference.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Count net carbs (total carbs minus fibre), not total carbs.
- Keep protein up — 1.6–2.2 g per kilogram of body weight a day.
- Drink water and replace salt: low-carb diets flush both out.

## Frequently asked questions

### What are keto macros?

The split of your daily calories between fat, protein and carbs. The standard keto split is 70% fat, 25% protein and 5% carbs — this calculator turns that into grams per day. Try it with your own numbers in the [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many carbs can I eat on keto?

Usually under 50 g of net carbs a day, and many people aim for 20–30 g. Net carbs are total carbs minus fibre. Try it with your own numbers in the [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How much protein do I need on keto?

About 1.6–2.2 g per kilogram of body weight a day. Too little protein costs muscle; the fat share is the flexible part of the diet. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### Is keto safe?

For most healthy adults it is safe short-term, but it is a medical diet for epilepsy and it does not suit everyone — pregnancy, kidney or liver disease, and some medications need a doctor's input first. Try it with your own numbers in the [Keto Calculator](/keto-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
